This is a recipe for oven-baked tandoori chicken that I have been experimenting with for the past month or so, and I almost have it perfected. This will be my 4th time making it, and I'm pretty confident that it will be fantastic this time. I like lots of ginger and garlic, so feel free to cut down on those ingredients if you don't like that zing.

Ingredients for chicken:

  • 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (¼ to ½ lbs each.)
  • 1 cup plain greek yogurt
  • ½ cup extra virgin olive oil
  • 5 cloves of garlic, minced
  • 1 medium-sized piece of fresh ginger root, shredded and then minced
  • 1 lemon, all of the juice, and some of the pulp
  • ½ yellow onion, sliced into rings
  • 1 tbsp salt
  • 2 tbsp Garam Masala
  • 2 tbsp cayenne pepper
  • 1 tbsp cumin
  • 1 tbsp coriander
  • 1 tbsp cardamom
  • 1 splash of vinegar for flavor (I just like a very small amount)

Note: If you don't have all of these spices, a place like Sprouts, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, or even King Soopers should have a Tandoori chicken spice packet for about $2.00

Ingredients for basmati rice

  • ½ cup basmati or brown long-grain rice
  • 1 cup water or chicken broth

Preparation:

  • Cut the chicken into small pieces, and slice the pieces down the middle, in order to help them absorb the flavor
  • Add the yogurt, spices, olive oil, lemon juice and the minced garlic and ginger into a bowl, and mix well.
  • After the mixture has been stirred, add the pieces of chicken to the bowl, and mix everything again. Be sure to coat the chicken well.
  • Place the bowl uncovered into the refrigerator, and let it marinate for about 4 hours (or overnight for a fuller flavor). Be sure to stir it every few hours, as the lemon juice and the olive oil will separate slightly. Marinating chicken

Cooking

  • Line a baking tray with aluminum foil, and place the chicken pieces onto the tray, making sure that the chicken is still well covered with yogurt
  • Place onion slices around the edges of the pan, to cook them slightly.
  • Pre-heat oven to 450˚
  • Place baking tray into the oven, and cook at 450˚ until the chicken starts to get a crispy look to it (his should take less than 20 minutes. The juices should run clear before removing from the oven.

  • Note: Cooking the chicken at a lower temperature for a longer period of time will actually dry out the chicken, and keep it from crisping up. the 450˚ flash cooking works incredibly well, and the chicken will be cooked thoroughly. At first I was afraid to bake the chicken for such a short period of time, but since the pieces are small, it doesn't take long at all.

  • Before the chicken starts cooking, boil the basmati rice and water/broth in a covered pot for about 40 minutes or until rice is soft. Remove the rice from the burner, fluff with a fork, and let it sit for about 30 minutes.

  • Remove chicken and onions from the oven, and place over basmati rice Add a dollop of yogurt and a few slices of cucumber to the plate as a garnish.

Enjoy! I'm making this tonight, so I'll edit this post and add a picture of the finished plate later this evening.
